# Compiler Errors, Decoded {.unnumbered}

Always compile with warnings on:

```bash
gcc -Wall -Wextra prog.c -o prog
```

::: {.callout-note}
Messages below were captured from a real compile. **Wording differs between compilers** — the lab machines use GNU gcc, this text came from clang. The part that always matters is **`file:line:column`**: go there first.
:::

## Read the FIRST error, not the last

One mistake often produces a cascade. Fix the top one and recompile; the rest frequently vanish.

## The common ones

| Message | Means | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `expected ';' at end of declaration` | missing semicolon — usually on the line **above** the one named | add `;` |
| `use of undeclared identifier 'y'` | name not declared, or misspelt, or out of scope | declare it; check spelling and braces |
| `call to undeclared function 'foo'` | no declaration above the call, or a missing `#include` | declare it, or add the header |
| `Undefined symbols … "_main"` | **linker**, not compiler: no `main` | you compiled a file with no `main` |
| `undefined reference to 'sqrt'` | declared but not linked | add `-lm` |
| `format specifies type 'int *' but the argument has type 'int'` | `scanf` missing `&` | `&x` |
| `format specifies type 'float *' … 'double *'` | `%f` for a `double` in `scanf` | use `%lf` |
| `sizeof on array function parameter` | the parameter is a pointer | pass the length separately |
| `& has lower precedence than ==` | precedence trap | parenthesise |
| `variable 'x' is uninitialized when used here` | read before any value was stored | initialise it |
| `control reaches end of non-void function` | a path with no `return` | return on every path |
| `unused variable 'x'` | harmless, but often a typo elsewhere | remove it, or use it |

## Compiler or linker?

| | |
|---|---|
| names a **file and line** | compiler — a syntax or type problem |
| says **undefined symbol / reference**, no line | linker — something was declared but never defined, or a library is missing |

## When it will not run

| | |
|---|---|
| `Permission denied` | `chmod +x prog` |
| `command not found` | write `./prog`, not `prog` |
| nothing happens | it is waiting for input — or an infinite loop; **Ctrl-C** |
| `Segmentation fault` | a bad pointer or an out-of-bounds index. No line number: compile with `-g` and narrow it with `printf` |
